description:
PREREQUISITE for String, IO, Integer/Float formatting -- every interesting primitive in those modules allocates.

An allocating extern needs *mut Process to reach heap.alloc_bitstring. That implicit
argument is derived from nothing; it is special-cased by symbol name in ~4 places:
  src/ir_codegen/runtime_syms.rs:69            wire signature
  src/compiler2/native_codegen/prim.rs:948     lower_extern_fz_binary_concat injects it
  src/ir_interp/extern_call.rs:190             interpreter call
  src/ir_interp/extern_call.rs:382             interpreter symbol address

prim.rs already carries 31 such rungs in one name-keyed if-chain before falling
through to lower_extern_generic. Non-allocating externs (fz_map_count,
fz_bitstring_valid_utf8, libc::close) cost nothing -- they take the generic path.

Cost if left alone: String needs 8-11 allocating primitives, Integer/Float/Atom 3,
Map 1-2, IO 1-2. At ~4 hand-edits each that is ~60-100 edits across three execution
paths, each an independent chance for three-path drift.

DONE = the extern contract carries the property, the generic path handles it once
across interp/JIT/AOT, and the if-chain in prim.rs is materially shorter. This is a
deletion as much as an addition -- adding a primitive must stop being a 4-site edit.

comments.text:
DESIGN, grounded in a read of the code (2026-09-07).

THE IF-CHAIN HAS TWO KINDS OF RUNG, and only one should become declared.
`native_codegen/prim.rs` special-cases 14 symbols by name plus the arithmetic
and comparison families. They are there for two different reasons:

  (a) "needs the process" -- the lowering's whole job is to prepend
      body.process_arg() and marshal the declared args. fz_binary_concat and
      fz_dbg_value are byte-for-byte the same shape:
          let process = body.process_arg();
          let call = body.call_named(SYM, &[process, ...args]);
          Ok(LowerOut::Strict(CodegenValue::AnyRef(result)))
      This is the shape EVERY String/IO/Integer/Float primitive will have, and
      it is what makes each new one a four-site edit today.

  (b) "is an intrinsic" -- the lowering emits something other than a call:
      fz_op_* become inline icmp/fcmp/fcvt, fz_send marshals a ValueRef and
      retargets to fz_send_ref, fz_spawn wraps a closure, fz_make_ref calls a
      differently-named raw symbol. These are not externs that happen to need a
      process; they are compiler intrinsics wearing extern syntax, and they
      should STAY hand-written.

So the ticket is (a) only. Do not try to collapse (b) -- that would be
conflating distinct-invariant lookalikes.

WHERE THE PROPERTY GOES. The ABI string is already parsed and, verified, NOT
validated against "C" (frontdoor.rs parse_extern_item captures it into `abi`
and nothing checks the value). So the declaration can carry it with no new
syntax:

    extern "C"  fn libc::close(integer) :: integer          plain C symbol
    extern "fz" fn fz_binary_concat(binary, binary) :: binary   receives the process

WHAT CHANGES.
  * frontdoor/extern_contract: thread the ABI through to the lowered extern
    decl as a boolean (or a small enum -- C vs FzRuntime).
  * lower_extern_generic (prim.rs:2273): it already builds the signature from
    decl.params/decl.ret via ExternTy, so this is prepending one I64 param and
    one process argument when the ABI says so.
  * ir_interp/extern_call.rs: the same, injecting runtime.cur_proc(). Today
    that file hand-matches each process-taking symbol twice (the call and the
    symbol-address table).
  * Delete the (a)-shaped lowerings that become redundant.

ACCEPTANCE. Adding a new allocating primitive should be: write the Rust fn,
register the symbol, declare it `extern "fz"` in the runtime library. No new
lowering function, no new interp match arm. Prove it by converting
fz_binary_concat and fz_dbg_value and showing the hand-written lowerings are
gone, with the quicksort and enum allocation goldens unmoved.

WATCH OUT: fz-5xp.19 -- an extern declared `(integer) :: float` mis-marshals on
BOTH doors today, taking the argument lane from the return type. Any lane work
here should fix or at least not step around that, since Float/String
primitives need float lanes.

title: Make 'needs the process heap' a declared extern property, not 31 name-keyed special cases
